findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices
findings.body: The matcher does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two things are wrong. First, the condition is inverted: the matcher returns false when the shortcut matches and true when it differs. Second, the grant shortcut sits at indices 4..6 of the 6-char prefix (`onrtac` gives `ac` at `substring(4,6)`), not 3..5. With the current code every event assertion (code-to-token, device, refresh, CIBA) accepts any wrong grant shortcut and would reject a correct one in most cases. The comment ('4th char') also disagrees with the indices used. The integration tests therefore don't validate the encoding.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check, so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId passes the constructor and later produces a token ID like `onrtac:null` in `encodeTokenId`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
findings.body: The test factory is built without `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into the refresh branch and dereferences the null `sessionFactory`. This throws an NPE, which the broad `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows, so the test passes without ever reaching the 'Unknown value for grant type' `IllegalArgumentException`. The test should catch `IllegalArgumentException` and provide a session factory stub or otherwise avoid the refresh path.

findings.title: Session type can be wrong for offline_access token requests
findings.body: The session type is derived from `userSession.isOffline()` at access-token creation time. On an initial `offline_access` login (code-to-token or direct grant) the access token is built from the online user session, and the offline session is created later for the refresh token. The online session may then be removed (see the `FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` handling in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase`). The token ID then says `on` although the online session no longer exists. This defeats the stated purpose of using the ID to choose which session type to look up, and the follow-up optimization #37662 would fail to find the session.

findings.title: Token creation fails hard when the grant type has no registered shortcut
findings.body: `encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` if `getShortcutByGrantType` returns null. The grant type comes from the request's `grant_type` form parameter via `Context.getGrantType()`. Any grant implementation or code path where the form parameter doesn't equal a registered factory ID would make access-token creation fail with a 500. Falling back to the `na` shortcut would be safer for a purely informational encoding.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of Context removed
findings.body: `Context(Context context)` was a public constructor in the SPI module. It is removed without any replacement or mention in the PR description. Third-party grant types or extensions that used it will break at compile time. The `grantType` field would not have been copied by it anyway.
